screen.grandcraft.choose_class: Choose your class — this choice is permanent!
screen.grandcraft.sheet.strength.tooltip: Heavy and two-handed weapons, and the size of your stamina pool. Nothing reads it yet — it is waiting on the weapon system.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.agility.tooltip: Light weapons, medium armour and archery, once those exist. Already in force: every stamina cost — attacking, dodging, jumping, sprinting, guarding — is %s%% of normal.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.constitution.too: How much punishment you can take. Already in force: %s armour, %s maximum health, and stamina recovers at %s%% of normal.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.arcane.tooltip: Mana, mana recovery and spell damage. Nothing reads it yet — it is waiting on magic.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.health.tooltip: What you can lose before you die. Constitution raises the ceiling but does not fill it — gaining it never heals you.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.stamina.tooltip: Spent on every committed action. Empty it and you are locked out until it recovers, which is the mistake the whole system is built around.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.mana.tooltip: Held for spells and abilities. Nothing spends it yet, so it sits full.
screen.grandcraft.stats.title: Stat Tuning
screen.grandcraft.stats.armour_per_const: Armour points gained per point of Constitution above 10, in hundredths — 50 means half a point each. Below 10 it costs armour instead. Minecraft caps total armour at 30 including worn gear, so a large value here is quietly clipped rather than refused.
screen.grandcraft.stats.health_per_const: Maximum health gained per point of Constitution above 10, in hundredths of a half-heart. Deliberately slight: Constitution is meant to make you harder to kill, not to make every fight longer. Raising it does not heal you — it raises the ceiling and leaves you to fill it.
screen.grandcraft.stats.stamina_regen_pe: Percent faster stamina recovery per point of Constitution above 10. This is how long you can keep making choices in a fight, so it is felt across a whole encounter rather than on any one action.
screen.grandcraft.stats.stamina_cost_per: Percent cheaper every stamina cost becomes per point of Agility above 10 — attacks, dodges, jumps, sprinting and blocking alike. The total is clamped so no amount of Agility can make an action free.
screen.grandcraft.stats.max_mana.tooltip: The size of the mana pool. Nothing spends mana yet; this exists so the magic layer arrives to a resource that already works. Zero switches mana off entirely.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_regen_per_s: Mana recovered per second. Set it low against a large pool to see the character sheet's mana actually climb — with nothing spending it, a full pool and a broken one look identical.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_regen_delay: Ticks of pause after spending mana before it starts coming back. Twenty ticks is one second. Has no effect until something can spend mana.
screen.grandcraft.game.title: GrandCraft Settings
screen.grandcraft.game.health_bars.toolt: Show a health bar above an entity for two seconds after it takes damage. Applies to every player on the server, and replaces that entity's name tag while it is up.
screen.grandcraft.game.combat_animations: Show attack wind-up, commitment and recovery as poses, so a swing can be read before it lands. Turning this off leaves the timings untouched — the attacks still happen, they just become invisible.
screen.grandcraft.config.title: Combat Tuning
screen.grandcraft.config.dodge_invulnera: How long a dodge makes attacks miss, starting on the very first tick. Long enough and a dodge always beats an attack already in flight; short enough and only a well-timed one does.
How long after the invulnerability ends before the roll can act again. This is the entire cost of dodging: dodge at the wrong moment and the next attack lands while you are still stuck in this.
screen.grandcraft.config.dodge_speed.too: How hard the roll launches, in hundredths of a block per tick. Physics decays it, so this sets how far the roll carries rather than a fixed distance. Very high values outrun collision and put actors through corners.
screen.grandcraft.config.dodge_cost.tool: What one dodge takes out of the pool. Set above an attack's cost so trading swings for dodges is a real decision rather than a free extra option.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_raise.too: How long the guard takes to come up, during which it stops nothing at all. This is the whole cost of blocking, paid in advance — the mirror of a dodge, which protects at once and charges afterwards. Long enough and only reading the wind-up early gets the guard up in time.
How long after letting go before the actor can act again. Stops the guard being flicked up and down for free, so dropping it to attack is a decision rather than a reflex.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_break.too: How long the stagger lasts when the pool runs dry behind a raised guard. The hit that empties it is still blocked; this is the punishment that follows. Always applied, unlike an ordinary stagger, because a guard break is a mistake made with your own resource.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_cost.tool: Stamina spent per point of damage absorbed, in hundredths — 250 means two and a half. Tune this against a whole fight, not one swing: blocking is continuous under pressure, so a cost that looks fair per hit can empty the pool in seconds.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_hold.tool: Stamina spent per second simply holding the guard up. Doing more than it looks: spending anything at all is what stops the pool regenerating behind a raised guard, so setting this to zero lets an actor recover while still blocking.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_arc.toolt: How far to either side of where the actor faces the guard reaches, so 180 covers everything and 90 covers only what is in front of the shoulders. Below about 120 the edge sits where a crowding attacker stands, and the same attack starts blocking or landing at random.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_slow.tool: How much movement speed is given up while the guard is up. The trade the verb is built on — safety for mobility — and what stops blocking being something to walk around behind.
screen.grandcraft.config.block_shield.to: What a shield multiplies the absorb cost by, against blocking bare-handed with a weapon. Below 100 a shield blocks more cheaply, which is the whole reason to carry one now that vanilla's own blocking is gone.
screen.grandcraft.config.startup.tooltip: Wind-up ticks before the blow lands. This is the window in which hitting the mob first cancels its attack, and the window in which you can step out of range to make it whiff. Long values make a mob easy to shut down, so pair a long wind-up with a wider Hit Window or the attack can never land.
screen.grandcraft.config.active.tooltip: Ticks during which the blow can actually connect. The mob commits at the start of its wind-up, so by the time this opens the target may have walked out of a reach of about 1.4 blocks — a long wind-up therefore needs a wide window, or the mob telegraphs, commits and whiffs every time. One hit only, however wide it is set.
screen.grandcraft.config.recovery.toolti: Ticks this actor is locked after swinging, before it can attack again. Nothing to do with regenerating health. Together with startup this is the whole attack cycle — nothing else paces it.
screen.grandcraft.config.stagger.tooltip: How long a hit staggers this actor: slowed and unable to attack. A second hit soon after gives half of this, and a third gives nothing, which is what stops a fast weapon locking a mob down forever.
screen.grandcraft.config.health.tooltip: Base stats: the starting point that later features add to rather than replace. Health, damage and speed are typed as whole percent of this actor's vanilla value, so 100 is unchanged and 150 is half again. A mob rolls its base once between min and max when it first spawns and keeps that roll for life — set min and max apart to get a spread of difficulties. Health and damage go to 2000, speed to 1000, though much past 300 speed the pathfinding stops keeping up.
screen.grandcraft.config.defence.tooltip: Armour points, not a multiplier — vanilla mobs have none, so there is nothing to multiply. Each point cuts incoming damage roughly 4%, to a maximum of 30.
screen.grandcraft.config.max_stamina.too: The size of this actor’s stamina pool. Every action is priced against it, so raising this makes an actor able to do more before it has to stop rather than making any single action cheaper. Set to 0 to turn stamina off for this actor entirely.
screen.grandcraft.config.regen.tooltip: Stamina refilled per second, once the delay below has passed. Nothing regenerates while stamina is being spent, so a sprint cost is really “how many seconds of sprinting the pool holds” and this is only how fast it comes back afterwards.
screen.grandcraft.config.regen_delay.too: Ticks after any spend before stamina starts coming back. Refreshed by every spend, so a continuous cost such as sprinting holds regeneration off for as long as it runs. Emptying the pool adds a further 20 ticks on top of this.
screen.grandcraft.config.attack_cost.too: Stamina spent per swing, charged whether it hit or missed. This is what makes a whiff a real mistake and what stops attacking being spammable. An actor with too little stamina to pay simply cannot attack.
screen.grandcraft.config.sprint_cost.too: Stamina drained per second of sprinting. Since nothing regenerates while it is being spent, pool divided by this is roughly how many seconds of continuous sprint the actor has. Sprinting stops the moment the pool empties. Set to 0 to leave sprinting free.
screen.grandcraft.config.jump_cost.toolt: Stamina spent per jump. Mobs are prevented from jumping when they cannot pay; the player is stopped by their own client, since a jump has already happened by the time the server hears about it. Set to 0 to leave jumping free.
screen.grandcraft.config.reset.tooltip: Restores the values on the open tab to their shipped defaults. Other tabs are left alone, and nothing is applied until you press Save.
commands.grandcraft.reclass.success: %s has been reset to Peasant and may choose a new class
screen.grandcraft.sheet.spend.tooltip: Spend one point on %s. Permanent — points cannot be moved once committed.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.pool_points.tool: Attribute points earned at milestone levels, waiting to be spent on the Health, Stamina or Mana pools. Use the buttons on the rows below. Buying a pool raises its ceiling and leaves you to fill it — it is not a heal.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.level.tooltip: Your Essence Power level. It rises by collecting Life Essence Orbs, which every mob drops when you kill it. Each level grants a stat point, and every fifth level also grants attribute points. Vanilla experience levels are a separate thing entirely and are not shown here.
screen.grandcraft.sheet.essence.tooltip: Essence collected towards your next level, against what that level costs. The difference between the two is how much more you need. Each level costs more than the one before it.
screen.grandcraft.stats.health_per_pool_: Maximum health gained per attribute point spent on Health, in half-hearts — 2 is one heart per point. Whole numbers here, unlike the per-Constitution figure above, because an attribute point is a rare deliberate purchase rather than a slight passive effect. Raising the ceiling does not heal you.
screen.grandcraft.stats.stamina_per_pool: Maximum stamina gained per attribute point spent on Stamina. At the default attack cost of 12, ten points here is most of an extra swing per purchase. The pool does not refill on purchase — the new room has to be earned back.
screen.grandcraft.stats.mana_per_pool_po: Maximum mana gained per attribute point spent on Mana. Nothing spends mana yet, so this is a placeholder for the magic layer to revisit. Has no effect at all while the mana pool above is set to zero.
screen.grandcraft.essence.level_up.point: %s stat point and %s attribute points to spend
screen.grandcraft.levels.title: Essence Power Tuning
screen.grandcraft.levels.base_cost.toolt: Essence needed for the very first level. At the default drop weights a kill is worth about 1.18 Essence, so 10 here is roughly nine kills. Cannot be zero: a level that costs nothing would be granted forever.
Extra Essence each level costs over the one before it. At 5, level 1 costs the base amount, level 5 costs four increases more, and so on. Set to 0 for a flat curve where every level costs the same.
screen.grandcraft.levels.drop_weight_1.t: How often a kill drops an orb worth 1 Essence, relative to the other two weights. These are shares rather than percentages, so 85/12/3 and 850/120/30 mean the same thing.
screen.grandcraft.levels.drop_weight_2.t: How often a kill drops an orb worth 2 Essence, relative to the other two weights. A larger orb is drawn larger, so raising this is visible as well as felt.
screen.grandcraft.levels.drop_weight_3.t: How often a kill drops an orb worth 3 Essence, relative to the other two weights. Kept rare by default so a big orb reads as a piece of luck.
screen.grandcraft.levels.stat_points_per: Points granted every level, spent on Strength, Agility, Constitution or Arcane. These are Stats, not the Health, Stamina and Mana pools — those are Attributes and are granted at milestones instead.
screen.grandcraft.levels.milestone_inter: How many levels apart the milestone levels are. A milestone grants attribute points on top of that level’s usual stat point. Cannot be zero.
screen.grandcraft.levels.pool_points_per: Points granted at each milestone level, spent on the Health, Stamina and Mana pools. These are Attributes, and are deliberately rarer than the stat points every level gives.
